writeup.headline: Analog Devices rates Buy on strong growth and margins, held back by high absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: ADI scores 66, just above the Buy edge, as strong business momentum outweighs a weak valuation score. Growth scores 87, with TTM revenue growth of 33.6% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 39.6% year on year, and growth sped up by 2.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 91 on a 65.8% gross margin, 35.5% operating margin and 35.6% FCF margin, with the diluted share count down 1.6% year on year. Trend is also strong at 84, with the price 15.5% above its 200-day average and 3.9% below its 52-week high. Against that, valuation scores only 22: multiples are high in absolute terms (14.9x sales, 42.0x FCF, 43.4x EV/EBIT, FCF yield 2.6 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and P/S and P/FCF are each more expensive than at 57 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: High absolute valuation leaves little room for disappointment, with P/S and P/FCF expensive against the company's own history.
The Q4 FY26 report on November 24 must meet the $4.3 billion +/- $100 million outlook to sustain momentum.
China's anti-dumping probe into US analog chips remains an open background risk.
Insider selling in early October with no purchases weighs on the news score of 48.
Cash covers only 0.25 of debt, and net debt is 1.38 times FCF.
what_would_change: A drop of just 2 points would move the rating to Hold, for example from a weaker trend score or slowing growth in the November report.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 14 more points, most plausibly from a better valuation score if prices fall or earnings grow into the multiples.
Positive guidance or analyst news from stronger sources could lift the news risk score of 48.
